method: Matching tempo is the ratio of the two BPM values: the playback rate needed is target divided by source, and the pitch fader setting is that ratio minus one, as a percentage, because the fader scales the nominal tempo linearly in percent. Varispeed playback changes pitch in proportion to speed, so the same ratio gives the key change: an octave is a 2:1 frequency ratio and holds 1200 cents, which makes the shift 1200 times the base-2 logarithm of the ratio, and semitones are that figure divided by 100. Fader travel is reported on a scale from 0 percent at the minus stop through 50 percent at the centre detent to 100 percent at the plus stop, so a setting of p percent on a range of r percent sits at 50 plus 50 p/r; travel outside that scale is clamped for display and the exact figure is also returned. The beat interval is 60000/BPM milliseconds. Two tracks running unsynced slip one beat after 60 divided by the absolute tempo difference in seconds, because their beat rates differ by that many beats per minute. Source and target tempo must be numbers from 20 to 300 BPM with at most ordinary decimal notation, the fader range must be one of ±6, ±8, ±10 or ±16 percent, and a missing, non-numeric or out-of-range value is rejected with an action message rather than defaulted. Keylock or master tempo holds the pitch while the tempo changes, so the key figure applies only where pitch follows speed: varispeed players, vinyl and turntables. Fader step size, the response curve of a particular player, pitch drift of the source material and any keylock artefacts are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Pitch and tempo: varispeed playback shifts pitch in proportion to speed, an octave is a 2:1 frequency ratio, and equal temperament divides the octave into 1200 cents
DJ pitch fader convention: the fader trims playback rate by a fixed percentage around the nominal tempo, with typical ranges of ±6, ±8, ±10 or ±16 percent and a centre detent at no change
